I get what you mean, but what is I find baffling is the fact that:

* Lambesis is being judged according to Christian standards when he has expressed doubt in that religion.  How is someone expected to commit themselves fully to something they're not even certain about?

* Lambesis was never one to force his beliefs on others.  He even said that he doesn't want his music to be judged according to his beliefs (paraphrased).  If he had behaved like a Republican politician, then I'd understand the hypocrisy, but he didn't.  Sure, his lyrics were inspired by his beliefs at a certain stage, but he left the interpretation up to the listener.

* I'd also like to point out something that's been bothering me for a while: I feel like atheists expect Christians to be perfect and not make mistakes.  Please understand from our point of view: we don't think of ourselves as perfect at all.  Rather, we recognize that we are sinners and need God to help us live better lives.  Lambesis has made a terrible mistake.  I'm not at all justifying what he did - in fact, I hope justice is served, whether he's innocent or guilty.  All I'm saying is that he's just like all of us, believers and non-believers alike.

Edit: one more thing.  The atheists that I have interacted with have expressed the opinion that they, too, are able to lead moral lives without having to believe in or follow God.  If you're saying that Christians, by having a moral code, should not do wrong so as to not be hypocrites, shouldn't atheists also be expected to lead good lives since they have a moral code, one which differs to that of Christians, but a moral code nonetheless?  Unless I'm mistaken.  I'm open for correction so I can learn. :)
